title: BrotherDS Claim Lifecycle v1
description: WBS-50.01. The claim lifecycle state machine the roadmap names: DRAFT, CHECKED, FROZEN, DECISION_USED, OUTCOME_AVAILABLE, RESOLVED, SCORED. Generic, no client-specific data: a claim's own content (what is being asserted, which evidence backs it) is deferred to later WBS-50 units (Claim Evidence references, MDM quality claims, mobile product claims) and is out of scope here, so this record carries only what the lifecycle itself needs -- identity, revision linkage, and state. Only the keyword subset scripts/claim_lifecycle.py actually enforces is used here: type, required, properties, enum, const, additionalProperties, matching the same enforced subset outcome-contract-v1, mobile-journey-contract-v1 and golden-master-contract-v1 document. The transition, mutation and revision rules the roadmap states (a FROZEN revision cannot be silently mutated, a correction creates a new revision linked by supersedes, the old revision remains auditable, scoring resolves the historical revision, never its rewritten successor) are cross-record rules no single record's schema can express; scripts/claim_lifecycle.py enforces them by hand.

schema_version.description: Which shape this record follows, so a reader never has to guess.

claim_id.description: Stable identifier shared by every revision of the same claim. A correction keeps this identifier; only revision_id changes.

revision_id.description: Identifier for this one revision. Unique per revision, never reused: a correction is a new record with a new revision_id, not a rewrite of this one.

state.description: Where this revision sits in the roadmap's own chain: DRAFT -> CHECKED -> FROZEN -> DECISION_USED -> OUTCOME_AVAILABLE -> RESOLVED -> SCORED. Each revision moves through this chain one step at a time; scripts/claim_lifecycle.py refuses any transition that is not the next state in this order.

supersedes.description: The revision_id of the earlier revision this one corrects, or null for a claim's first revision. A non-null value must name a different revision_id than this record's own (a revision cannot supersede itself).
